Interface SecretStore

All Known Implementing Classes:
Atecc608
public interface SecretStore
Named secrets read from a secure element. Values are never stored on the SD card or in the firmware image. Code on the board can read them; physical access to the board is the trust boundary. A missing, empty, or unverifiable secret is reported as missing, and no implementation falls back to a plaintext copy.

  • Method Details

    • read

      int read(String key, byte[] buffer)
      Copies the value of key into buffer and returns its length, or a negative value when the key is unknown, the secret is missing, the chip does not answer or fails its checksum, or the value is longer than buffer. Allocates nothing; buffer is written only on success.

    • write

      int write(String key, byte[] value, int length)
      Stores value[0..length) under key, replacing whatever was there, and returns length. A length of 0 clears the name. Returns a negative value when the name is unknown, the bytes do not fit, or the store refuses the write (for example a locked zone or a missing chip). A failed write may leave the name partly rewritten, so the caller should write it again. Writes come from provisioning code, not from programs that only read secrets.

    • clear

      int clear(String key)
      Empties key, so that a later read(String, byte[]) reports it missing. Returns 0 on success, or -1 when the name is unknown or the store refuses the write.

    • clearAll

      int clearAll()
      Empties every name the store knows, which are the names in its table; a slot that the table does not name is not touched. Tries every name even after a failure. Returns 0 when all were cleared, or -1 when any failed.

    • getString

      @Nullable String getString(String key)
      Returns the value of key as a String, or null when it is missing. Allocates one String, so call it once at startup.
